request.statement:
Validate and flatten a namespace-aware robot forest with coupled joint limits.

Define `import_robot_forest(links, joints)`.

`links` is a sequence of canonical link names. `joints` is a sequence of 10-tuples `(name, parent_ref, child_ref, kind, lower, upper, payload, mimic_ref, multiplier, offset)`. `payload` is copied to the result. `mimic_ref` is either `None` or a joint reference; `multiplier` is one of `-1, 0, 1`, and `offset` is an integer. They are ignored when `mimic_ref` is `None`.

Canonical names consist of nonempty `/`-separated alphanumeric-or-underscore segments, without a leading `/`. Names are canonical unless stated otherwise. A reference is canonical and relative, or starts with `/` and is absolute. Input syntax and types satisfy these rules. `kind` is one of `"fixed"`, `"revolute"`, `"prismatic"`, `"floating"`, `"spherical"`.

Resolve a reference against the complete relevant name set. `/x` resolves only to `x`. For a relative reference in declaration `a/b/j`, try `a/b/ref`, then `a/ref`, then `ref`, choosing the first existing name.

First scan links. On the first duplicate at index `i`, return `("ERROR", "DUPLICATE_LINK", i, name)`.

Then scan joints structurally. For each index, check in order: duplicate joint name, unresolved parent, unresolved child, child already owned by an earlier joint, and creation of a directed body cycle. Return respectively:
`("ERROR", "DUPLICATE_JOINT", i, name)`,
`("ERROR", "UNKNOWN_PARENT", i, parent_ref)`,
`("ERROR", "UNKNOWN_CHILD", i, child_ref)`,
`("ERROR", "MULTIPLE_PARENTS", i, child_name)`, or
`("ERROR", "CYCLE", i, name)`.

Only after all structural checks succeed, scan mimic declarations by input index. A mimic reference resolves against all joint names. Check in order:

1. Unresolved reference: `("ERROR", "UNKNOWN_MIMIC", i, mimic_ref)`.
2. Either joint is not revolute or prismatic, or their kinds differ: `("ERROR", "INVALID_MIMIC", i, name)`.
3. Adding the dependency would create a mimic cycle, including self-reference: `("ERROR", "MIMIC_CYCLE", i, name)`.

A joint's own interval is `(lower, upper)` only for revolute or prismatic joints with both bounds present and `lower <= upper`; otherwise it is unrestricted. A mimicking joint has coordinate `q = multiplier * source_q + offset`. Its effective interval is the intersection of its own interval and the image of the source's effective interval. An unrestricted source contributes no interval when the multiplier is nonzero, but contributes `(offset, offset)` when it is zero.

Evaluate joints only after their sources; among currently eligible joints use input index order. If an intersection is empty, immediately return `("ERROR", "LIMIT_CONFLICT", i, name)`.

On success return `("OK", forests)`. Roots are lexicographic. Each forest is a preorder tuple of `(link_name, incoming)`. Root `incoming` is `None`; otherwise it is `(joint_name, kind, effective_interval, driver, payload)`, where `driver` is `None` or `(resolved_source_name, multiplier, offset)`. Order children by `(joint_name, child_link_name)`. Every link appears once.

There are at most 200,000 links and joints and 4,000,000 total name/reference characters. Use only the standard library. Do not perform I/O, access external state, mutate arguments, or depend on nondeterminism.
